``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {#key-terms .callout-note collapse="true"} ## Key terms | Term | Definition | |---|---| | Unemployment rate | "The unemployment rate is the number of unemployed persons expressed as a percentage of the labour force. The unemployment rate for a particular group (age, gender, marital status, etcetera.) is the number unemployed in that group expressed as a percentage of the labour force for that group." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 9) | | Employment | "Number of persons who, during the reference week, worked for pay or profit, or performed unpaid family work or had a job but were not at work due to own illness or disability, personal or family responsibilities, labour dispute, vacation, or other reason. Those persons on layoff and persons without work but who had a job to start at a definite date in the future are not considered employed." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 7) | | Participation rate | "The participation rate is the number of labour force participants expressed as a percentage of the population 15 years of age and over. The participation rate for a particular group (age, gender, marital status, etcetera.) is the number of labour force participants in that group expressed as a percentage of the population for that group." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 10) | | Labour force | "Number of civilian, non-institutionalized persons 15 years of age and over who, during the reference week, were employed or unemployed." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0459-01, footnote 6) | | Employment Insurance regular beneficiaries | "The number of beneficiaries represents a count of persons who qualified for employment insurance benefits during the Labour Force Survey reference week, usually containing the 15th day of the month." "Includes people who receive regular income benefits whether or not they participate in one of three employment benefit programs, namely Skills Development Program, Job Creation Partnerships Program and Self-employment Program." (Statistics Canada, table 14-10-0454-01, footnotes 4 and 1) | | Active businesses | "Active businesses are those businesses that reported having one or more employees in a given month." (Statistics Canada, table 33-10-0270-01, footnote 4) | | Openings | "Opening businesses are businesses that transition from having no employees in the previous month to having at least one employee in the current month. These instances occur when a new, small firm begins, when a large firm opens a new establishment or when a seasonal firm re-opens." (Statistics Canada, table 33-10-0270-01, footnote 1) | | Non-residential | "the total value of building permits is obtained by summing the following elements: residential, industrial, commercial and institutional." (Statistics Canada, table 34-10-0292-01, footnote 7) | | New Housing Price Index | "The New Housing Price Index (NHPI) is a monthly series that measures changes over time in the builders' selling prices of new residential houses, where detailed specifications pertaining to each house remain the same between two consecutive periods." "The index base period, for which the New Housing Price Index (NHPI) equals 100, is December 2016." (Statistics Canada, New Housing Price Index survey description; table 18-10-0205-01, footnote 3) | | Housing starts | A start is "the beginning of construction work on a building. This is usually when the concrete has been poured for the whole of the footing around the structure or an equivalent stage where a basement will not be part of the structure." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Single | "a building containing 1 dwelling unit, which is completely separated on all sides from any other dwelling or structure." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Single-Detached") | | Semi-detached | "1 of 2 dwellings located side-by-side in a building, adjoining no other structure and separated by a common or party wall extending from ground to roof." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Row | "a 1-family dwelling unit in a row of 3 or more attached dwellings separated by a common or party wall extending from ground to roof." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Row (Townhouse)") | | Apartment | "all dwellings other than those described above, including structures commonly known as stacked townhouses, duplexes, triplexes, double duplexes and row duplexes." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Apartment and Other") | | Intended market | "the tenure in which the unit is being marketed." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Rental | "a dwelling constructed for rental purposes, regardless of who finances the structure." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Condo | "an individual dwelling unit which is privately owned, but where the building and/or the land are collectively owned by all dwelling unit owners." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption, "Condominium") | | Homeowner | "a residence where the owner owns the dwelling and lot outright." (CMHC, Survey methodologies: Starts and Completions and Market Absorption) | | Vacancy rate | "A unit is considered vacant if, at the time of the survey, the unit is physically unoccupied and available for immediate rental." The survey covers "all row projects and apartment structures with three or more units" that are "privately initiated". (CMHC, Methodology for Rental Market Survey) | | Average rent | "The rent refers to the actual amount tenants pay for their unit. No adjustments are made for the inclusion or exclusion of amenities and services." (CMHC, Methodology for Rental Market Survey) | | Same-sample rent change | "Percentage change in average rent provides an estimate of rent level movement by eliminating the compositional effects of new structures, conversions and survey sample rotation. The estimate is based on existing rental structures that were common to the survey sample for both the previous year and the current Rental Market Survey year." (CMHC, Methodology for Rental Market Survey) | | Net non-permanent residents | "A non-permanent resident refers to a person from another country with a usual place of residence in Canada and who has a work or study permit or who has claimed refugee status (asylum claimant, protected person or member of related groups). Family members living with work or study permit holders are also included unless these family members are already Canadian citizens, landed immigrants (permanent residents), or non-permanent residents themselves." (Statistics Canada, table 17-10-0153-01, footnote 13) | | Crime Severity Index | "The Crime Severity Index (CSI) measures changes in the level of severity of crime in Canada from year to year. In the index, all crimes are assigned a weight based on their seriousness. The level of seriousness is based on actual sentences handed down by the courts in all provinces and territories. More serious crimes are assigned higher weights, less serious offences lower weights." "The crime severity index includes all Criminal Code violations including traffic, as well as drug violations and all Federal Statutes." (Statistics Canada, table 35-10-0026-01, footnotes 20 and 16) | | Violent crime | "The violent crime severity index includes all Incident-based Uniform Crime Reporting Survey (UCR2) violent violations." (Statistics Canada, table 35-10-0026-01, footnote 18) | | Non-violent crime | "The non-violent crime severity index includes all non-violent Criminal Code violations including traffic, as well as drug violations and all Federal Statutes." initiated rental structures of three or more units in centres of 10,000 people or more | 2026-09-25 | ### Reliability | Items of note | |---| | **Kitchener - Cambridge - Waterloo CMA:** every chart except the population charts shows the census metropolitan area for the Region, because it is the smallest area these tables publish. The CMA is six of the Region's seven districts; Wellesley Township, about 2% of the Region's people, is left out and nothing outside the Region is included. The Labour Force Survey tables use 2021 CMA boundaries throughout. The Crime Severity Index and the incident rates are compiled from police services, and Statistics Canada notes that "the boundaries for the policing-based CMAs do not always fully align with the standard CMA geographic units". The two population charts use the census division, which is the whole Region. (tables 14-10-0459, 14-10-0458, 14-10-0454, 33-10-0270, 34-10-0292, 18-10-0205, 35-10-0026, 35-10-0177; CMHC) | | **Labour Force Survey:** the unemployment, participation, employment and labour-force figures, overall and by age, are estimates from a monthly survey of about 65,000 households, and a CMA's share of that sample is small; "estimates are based on smaller sample sizes the more detailed the table becomes, which could result in lower data quality", and estimates below 1,500 people are suppressed. The CMA figures are three-month moving averages, which Statistics Canada publishes to steady them. The overall unemployment rate, participation rate and employment charts draw the Region's 95% confidence interval from the published standard errors; the tables by age publish none. Seasonally adjusted series have "seasonal movements ... eliminated" but still contain irregular movements; the figures by age are not seasonally adjusted, so their lines rise and fall with the seasons. (tables 14-10-0459, 14-10-0458, 14-10-0017) | | **Labour Force Survey, figures too unreliable to publish:** Statistics Canada rates some of the Region's monthly figures by age F, "too unreliable to be published"; within the five years shown, that is the unemployment rate of people aged 55 to 64 for November 2023, which leaves a gap in the Region's line on that chart. (table 14-10-0458) | | **Employment Insurance revisions:** "Estimates for the current and previous month are subject to revision", so the last two months on the chart may change. (table 14-10-0454) | | **Business openings and closures:** these are experimental estimates from payroll records. Statistics Canada flags the Region's count of active businesses "use with caution" (E) for June 2021 and January 2022; those counts are not used, which leaves gaps in the Region's lines on the two per-100-businesses charts. The counts of openings and closures themselves are not flagged, so the Region-only charts have no gaps. (table 33-10-0270) | | **Population estimates are revised:** the latest year's population and components are preliminary and the two or three before it updated; each is revised as later data come in, the last when the next census is counted. (tables 17-10-0152, 17-10-0153, 17-10-0148, 17-10-0005) | | **Crime Severity Index and incident rates:** police-reported crime only; the previous year's figures are revised each year; the index weights were updated with 2022 data; and some older records were imputed from the aggregate survey. (tables 35-10-0026, 35-10-0177) | | **Railway police undercount, 2021 and 2022:** the "Other Federal Statutes" incidents the Canadian Pacific Railway Police reported for 2021 and 2022 "may be an undercount" and "should be interpreted with caution". They are part of all violations, so of the overall and non-violent incident rates. (table 35-10-0177) | | **CMHC housing starts:** CMHC counts starts every month in census metropolitan areas and census agglomerations, the centres of 10,000 people or more; smaller places are counted only quarterly, by sample. The Ontario and Canada figures here are for those centres, and are divided by the population living in them. | | **CMHC Rental Market Survey:** a survey each October of a sample of privately initiated rental apartment and row structures of three or more units, in centres of 10,000 people or more. CMHC rates each figure's reliability; every figure charted is rated excellent or very good. A figure rated "Fair (Use with Caution)" would not be shown. | ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Reproducibility **Reproduce the page**: get the code and data for this page from [`vital-statistics/`](https://github.com/gpberber/chartingwaterlooregion/tree/master/vital-statistics) on GitHub. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` R version: R version 4.5.3 (2026-03-11 ucrt) OS: Windows 11 x64 (build 26200) Rendered: 2026-09-25 Quarto: 1.9.38 package version date source conflicted 1.2.0 2023-02-01 CRAN (R 4.2.3) dplyr 1.2.1 2026-04-03 CRAN (R 4.5.2) forcats 1.0.1 2025-09-25 CRAN (R 4.5.3) ggiraph 0.9.6 2026-02-21 CRAN (R 4.5.3) ggplot2 4.0.3 2026-04-22 CRAN (R 4.5.3) ggtext 0.2.0 2026-08-28 CRAN (R 4.5.3) gt 1.3.0 2026-01-22 CRAN (R 4.5.3) gtExtras 0.6.2 2026-01-17 CRAN (R 4.5.3) here 1.0.2 2025-09-15 CRAN (R 4.5.3) janitor 2.2.1 2024-12-22 CRAN (R 4.5.3) lubridate 1.9.5 2026-02-04 CRAN (R 4.5.3) patchwork 1.3.2 2025-08-25 CRAN (R 4.4.3) purrr 1.2.2 2026-04-10 CRAN (R 4.5.2) readr 2.2.0 2026-02-19 CRAN (R 4.5.3) scales 1.4.0 2025-04-24 CRAN (R 4.5.3) shadowtext 0.1.6 2025-08-24 CRAN (R 4.5.3) stringr 1.6.0 2025-11-04 CRAN (R 4.5.3) tibble 3.3.1 2026-01-11 CRAN (R 4.5.2) tidyr 1.3.2 2025-12-19 CRAN (R 4.5.3) tidyverse 2.0.0 2023-02-22 CRAN (R 4.5.2) ``` ::: ::: :::
